content:
#1 Due to the acceptance of plenitudinous platonism—at least in concept—the philosophy of mathematics has transitioned from the existential to the functional. Monism and pluralism are not the disbelief or belief of incompatible models of mathematics; is it more useful for an in-depth research of mathematical objects in one mathematical model or is it more useful for an in-passing research of mathematical objects in multiple compatible or incompatible mathematical models is the modern tension of the monist and the pluralist. Intuitionism and classicalism are not the disbelief of classicalism or intuitionism proofs; is it more useful for constructible proofs or classical proofs is too the modern tension of intuitionism and classicalism. I am a mathematical humanist against the mathematical pragmatists' computer or artificial intelligence based-proofs in the same light. Mathematics is in a pairwise disjoint partition of teleological and etiological; it should be both. The teleologian regards Newton's mathematics as applied and Leibniz's mathematics as pure, the etiologian regards Tao's mathematics as applied due to the use of AI and computers and Galois's mathematics as pure; I demand it be both teleological and etiological—so I introduce full-blooded pure mathematics.

Perhaps I'm too romantic, but mathematics to me and most mathematicians I know seems to be a liberal arts over a STEM field, that there are computer generated and artificial intelligence generated proofs of theorems that are hundreds of lines of code that are not comprehensible to us seems to defeat the point of mathematics as anything but an applied discipline. Thoughts on this distinction?
subject: On The Definition of Pure Mathematics

content: #2 Note that I am not against proof checkers, that is an artificial intelligence peer review. I mean the ones that act as collaborators or even the generators. There is the artist that uses artificial intelligence to enhance their art and the artist that enhances the artificial intelligence's art, one I find acceptable the other I do not (in terms of liberal art).
subject: On The Definition of Pure Mathematics

content:
#3 To me, mathematics is applied when it’s used in other non-mathematics fields; it is pure when it’s only used in mathematics.

most mathematicians I know seems to be a liberal arts over a STEM field

A lot of theoretical physics such as quantum gravity or force unification these days seems more like a liberal arts field than a STEM field as well, because of the lack of any connection to scientific experiment. It marks the point where physics stops being a science and returns to being natural philosophy, and the questions of quantum gravity and force unification has all the hallmarks of being an unresolvable philosophical question for the foreseeable future.

The mathematics used in quantum gravity or force unification is still applied mathematics regardless to me, it’s just applied to philosophy rather than science. Back in the day when I used to consider physics a subfield of science, I would have definitely considered any mathematics used only in quantum gravity or force unification to have been pure mathematics, because it’s not science. But these days, physics to me is more than a subfield of science, it is a field that has its scientific and philosophical subareas. However, many others still consider physics to be a subfield of science, so that debate over whether mathematics used in theoretical physics with no connection to the real world should count as applied or pure still rages on.

that there are computer generated and artificial intelligence generated proofs of theorems that are hundreds of lines of code that are not comprehensible to us seems to defeat the point of mathematics as anything but an applied discipline.

AI and the computer in this context is just a tool to generate and verify proofs of theorems, it doesn’t change anything about whether the theorem is pure or applied mathematics, because generating and proving theorems doesn’t change the status of whether it’s being applied in non-mathematical contexts or not. If a large language model constructs a formal definition of the Feynman path integral, that does not change the fact that the Feynman path integral is applied mathematics. Likewise, if a large language model starts proving theorems about V = L, it doesn’t change the fact that the V = L axiom in set theory is pure mathematics.

Same goes in philosophy when people use large language models to write philosophical papers, it doesn’t change whether the philosophy itself is being applied in non-philosophical contexts or not.

The only new applied mathematics here with large language models is the mathematics behind the architecture of the large language model (transformers, etc).
subject: On The Definition of Pure Mathematics

content: #4 Then if it is not a matter of purity, what is the modern philosophical debate that composes these question?
subject: On The Definition of Pure Mathematics

content:
#5

Then if it is not a matter of purity, what is the modern philosophical debate that composes these question?

The use of AI and computers more broadly in proof generation and proof verification is a question of the philosophy of mathematical practice, of mathematical values and ethics. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy has an article on this topic of the philosophy of mathematical practice:

https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/mathematical-practice/

Note that section 3.1 talks about a different kind of purity in mathematics that might be relevant to the AI discussion. But that purity is not the same as purity in the debate over pure vs applied mathematics; it’s talking about pure vs impure proof methods.

See also these two papers:

  1. Mathematical methods and human thought in the age of AI by Tanya Klowden and Terence Tao
  2. Mathematics in the age of AI by Terence Tao.
subject: On The Definition of Pure Mathematics

content: #6 Благодарю вас! I'll be interested to read them. Similar to Grothedieck's rising wave and Galois's Group Theory; is brute forcing the solution setting us up for failure in the future when we need such a novel collaboration or contribution.
